subject: Clarify DPA roles, SCCs, and export controls for Pioneer Health
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@pioneerhealth.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, contracts@pioneerhealth.com
Date: 2028-09-30T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: DPA redlines + SCCs follow-up

Hi Irene / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are our proposed redlines to the DPA and the SCCs annex — we highlighted a few items that are blocking internal procurement:

- Role delegation: Pioneer expects the processor/processor-of-processor callout for logging and telemetry that your order form currently lists as "operational data". We need explicit processor/processor roles in the DPA.
- Export controls / transfer impact: given some data originates in the EU, we want a Transfer Impact Addendum or a commitment to specific SCC versioning.
- Subprocessors: included a short CSV of required subprocessors we need visibility on.

Attached: PioneerHealth_DPA_Redlines_2028-09-30.docx, SCCs_Annex_v4.pdf, Subprocessor_List_Pioneer_2028-09-28.csv

Can you confirm who from Redwood will own redline responses (legal v privacy)? Also give us an ETA for a mark-up and whether you can accept limited carveouts for export controls.

Best,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Procurement — Pioneer Health
sofia.ramos@pioneerhealth.com

--

I attached the files they sent. Prefer a short redline + one-pager we can send back with supporting evidence (SOC2 scope, export controls note).

Thanks,

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redlines + SCCs follow-up

Thanks for the ping — I reviewed Pioneer’s markup. High-level legal position and proposed next steps below: 

1) Roles and responsibilities: Pioneer is right to ask for explicit role language. Proposed approach: we accept processor role for runtime logging and support telemetry but will keep responsibility for model training/feature development in the MSA scope (controller relationship remains with Pioneer for PII they upload). I will draft exact DPA text to call out "Processor" duties for inference telemetry + security logs and include a short example table of typical activities.

2) SCCs and Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): we should not commit to a perpetual version tie to a single SCC iteration. Instead propose: we accept execution of the latest EC-approved SCCs at time of signature and agree to provide a TIA summary that documents technical & contractual safeguards (KMS regioning, pseudonymization where used, access controls). I will draft a 1-page TIA summary we can include as an annex.

3) Subprocessors: we can provide the list in the CSV but request a 30-day notice for additions and a standard objection window; for critical subprocessors we can route to a data-locality exception process.

4) Narrow carveouts: Pioneer’s redline includes a broad export-control carveout. Recommend we offer operational mitigations instead of carveouts: regional routing preference, per-customer KMS key option, and documentation of export-control assessments.

I will produce a redline with tracked changes and a proposed TIA annex draft by COB tomorrow. Karthik — can you provide a 1-paragraph privacy summary we can include in the TIA? Ben — if we want to keep momentum, we should schedule a 30-min call with Pioneer to walk through the anchor points.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-01T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redlines + SCCs follow-up

Adding the privacy POV — short summary for the TIA annex that Laura can paste in: 

- Data flows: Pioneer will be controller for patient PII they submit; Redwood acts as processor for inference and associated telemetry. Data residency: production inference happens in us-west-2; we can offer EU routing for EU-origin sessions on Dedicated or via Private deployment.
- Technical safeguards: per-customer KMS support (optional), KV-cache TTL controls to reduce retention, and masking/pseudonymization guidelines for model inputs we recommend for PH.
- Residual risk & mitigations: for export-control sensitivity we recommend a combination of routing + contractually bound handling; where customers require stricter control we can propose a Transfer Impact Addendum documenting technical configs and operational playbooks.

I attached a short draft annex (Privacy_Annex_Draft_2028-10-01.docx) with schema for the TIA and a checkbox list for evidence items (SOC2 scope, subprocessor attestations).

Karthik Iyer
Privacy & Trust — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

[attachment: Privacy_Annex_Draft_2028-10-01.docx]
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: irene.choi@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-02T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + SCCs follow-up

Hi Sofia — thanks for sending these over and apologies for the back-and-forth. Quick response and proposed path: 

1) Timeline: Redwood can return a consolidated redline + TIA summary by EOD Tuesday (2028-10-03). If that works for Pioneer we can aim to close procurement the week after.

2) What we'll send: Laura will send a tracked-changes DPA (showing processor/processor-of-processor language), Karthik’s 1-paragraph privacy summary in the TIA annex, and our subprocessor list with the 30-day add notice clause.

3) Short-term compromise on export controls: we cannot accept an open carveout. We propose: (a) regional routing preference for EU-origin data, (b) optional customer-managed KMS for keys, and (c) a short TIA annex documenting controls and mitigations — if Pioneer still needs stricter terms we can propose a Dedicated/Private deployment pricing path that meets those requirements.

4) Next step: would Pioneer accept a 30-minute call on Wed (10/03) at 10am PT to walk the redline and TIA? If so, contracts@pioneerhealth.com please send a calendar invite.

If that timeline works, we will attach the redline package to the reply and include a one-page evidence checklist (SOC2 in-scope items, export-control assessment summary).

Best,
